## [pnpm 12 Alpha 18](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/releases/tag/v12.0.0-alpha.18)
*GitHub Releases · pnpm* | 22/07/2026 | Score: 0.70
Tags: creative_workflow

> <h2>Minor Changes</h2> <ul> <li> <p>The first release of a package now publishes the version written in its manifest verbatim, instead of bumping off it. <code>pnpm version -r</code> and <code>pnpm change status</code> check the registry for each release's current version; when that version is not yet published, the package debuts at it and its pending changesets apply only from the next release. A newly added package seeded at <code>1100.0.0</code> with a <code>minor</code> changeset is therefore published as <code>1100.0.0</code> rather than skipping straight to <code>1100.1.0</code>.</p> </li> <li> <p><code>pnpm version</code> now supports the npm-style bump forms: <code>pnpm version <major|minor|patch|premajor|preminor|prepatch|prerelease></code> and <code>pnpm version <exact-version></code> (also recursively with <code>-r</code>), with <code>--preid</code>, <code>--allow-same-version</code>, <code>--message</code>, <code>--no-git-tag-version</code>, <code>--no-commit-hooks</code>, <code>--sign-git-tag</code>, <code>--tag-version-prefix</code>, and <code>--json</code>. The bump runs the <code>preversion</code>/<code>version</code>/<code>postversion</code> lifecycle scripts and records the new version as a git commit and tag.</p> </li> <li> <p>Added recursive workspace support to <code>pnpm outdated</code>. <code>pnpm list</code> and <code>pnpm ll</code> now inspect all workspace projects by default, matching the TypeScript CLI.</p> </li> <li> <p>Made recursive <code>pnpm rebuild</code> honor workspace filters with shared and dedicated lockfiles.</p> </li> <li> <p>Made <code>pnpm why</code> and <code>pnpm peers</code> recursive by default in workspaces. Recursive peer checks now honor workspace filters, and recursive <code>why</code> can inspect the active project when a workspace uses dedicated lockfiles.</p> </li> <li> <p>Added a <code>--changeset</code> flag to <code>pnpm update</code>. Set <code>update.changeset</code> to <code>true</code> in <code>pnpm-workspace.yaml</code> to enable this behavior by default, and use <code>--no-changeset</code> to override the setting for one update. After the update completes, pnpm writes a <code>.changeset/pnpm-update-<suffix>.md</code> file declaring a patch bump for every workspace package whose <code>dependencies</code> or <code>optionalDependencies</code> were changed by the update and a major bump when <code>peerDependencies</code> changed, including packages that consume an updated catalog entry via the <code>catalog:</code> protocol. Private packages, packages without a name, and packages listed in the <code>ignore</code> array of <code>.changeset/config.json</code> are skipped. If <code>.changeset/config.json</code> does not exist, a warning is printed and no changeset is generated.</p> </li> <li> <p>Added GitHub Actions dependencies to <code>pnpm outdated</code> and interactive <code>pnpm update</code>. Non-interactive updates can include them with <code>--include-github-actions</code> or by setting <code>update.githubActions</code> to <code>true</code> in <code>pnpm-workspace.yaml</code>. Updated actions are pinned to exact commit hashes with their release tags preserved in comments.</p> </li> </ul> <h2>Patch Changes</h2> <ul> <li> <p>Fixed <code>pnpm install</code> rewriting unrelated <code>pnpm-lock.yaml</code> entries after a small manifest change — for example, removing one dev dependency could bump other packages' open-range dependencies (such as jest's <code>@types/node: '*'</code>) to their newest versions <a href="https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/pull/13193" data-hovercard-type="pull_request" data-hovercard-url="/pnpm/pnpm/pull/13193/hovercard">pnpm/pnpm#13193</a>. Three resolution-reuse gaps caused still-satisfied lockfile entries to be re-resolved from the registry:</p> <ul> <li>Direct dependencies using the <code>catalog:</code> protocol were compared against the lockfile in their resolved-range form, so every catalog-managed dependency looked changed on every install, and any package depending on one was re-resolved.</li> <li>Auto-installed (hoisted) peer dependencies were also treated as changed direct dependencies on every install.</li> <li>When a package had to resolve freshly but landed on the version the lockfile already recorded, its dependency subtree was still re-resolved instead of being reused, drifting open ranges pinned by the lockfile.</li> </ul> </li> <li> <p><code>pnpm install</code>, <code>pnpm add</code>, <code>pnpm update</code>, and <code>pnpm remove</code> now support recursive (<code>-r</code>) and filtered (<code>--filter</code>) execution in workspaces configured with one lockfile per project (<code>sharedWorkspaceLockfile: false</code>), instead of failing with <code>ERR_PNPM_RECURSIVE_SHARED_LOCKFILE_UNSUPPORTED</code>. Each selected project is installed independently against its own <code>pnpm-lock.yaml</code>, <code>node_modules</code>, and virtual store, matching pnpm.</p> </li> <li> <p>Global commands (<code>pnpm add -g</code>, <code>pnpm runtime set -g</code>, ...) now create a missing global bin directory instead of failing with <code>ERR_PNPM_PNPM_DIR_NOT_WRITABLE</code>, and the universal <code>--silent</code> / <code>-s</code> shorthands for <code>--reporter=silent</code> (e.g. <code>pnpm store path --silent</code>) are supported again.</p> </li> <li> <p><code>pnpm unlink</code> now reinstalls through the selection-aware install pipeline, matching pnpm: it honors <code>-r</code> / <code>--filter</code>, installs recursively by default inside a workspace, and supports both a shared workspace lockfile and one lockfile per project (<code>sharedWorkspaceLockfile: false</code>). Previously it always reinstalled only the active project.</p> </li> <li> <p>Added <code>update</code> and <code>audit</code> settings sections to <code>pnpm-workspace.yaml</code>, superseding the awkwardly named <code>updateConfig</code>, <code>auditConfig</code>, and top-level <code>auditLevel</code> settings:</p> <div class="highlight highlight-source-yaml notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="update: ignoreDeps: # was updateConfig.ignoreDependencies - webpack - "@babel/*" audit: level: high # was auditLevel ignore: # was auditConfig.ignoreGhsas - GHSA-xxxx-yyyy-zzzz"><pre><span class="pl-ent">update</span>: <span class="pl-ent">ignoreDeps</span>: <span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> was updateConfig.ignoreDependencies</span> - <span class="pl-s">webpack</span> - <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>@babel/*<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> <span class="pl-ent">audit</span>: <span class="pl-ent">level</span>: <span class="pl-s">high </span><span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> was auditLevel</span> <span class="pl-ent">ignore</span>: <span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> was auditConfig.ignoreGhsas</span> - <span class="pl-s">GHSA-xxxx-yyyy-zzzz</span></pre></div> <p><code>update.ignoreDeps</code> lists dependency name patterns that <code>pnpm update</code> and <code>pnpm outdated</code> should skip. <code>audit.level</code> and <code>audit.ignore</code> tune <code>pnpm audit</code>.</p> <p>The deprecated <code>updateConfig</code>, <code>auditConfig</code>, and <code>auditLevel</code> settings keep working until the next major version. When both a new section value and its deprecated counterpart are set, the new section takes precedence and a warning is printed. Both the TypeScript CLI and the Rust config surface (pacquet) recognize the new sections.</p> </li> </ul>
